therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: cardiopulmonary function modulation under hypoxic stress
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Healthy subjects exposed to high altitude hypoxia
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Peak Exercise Oxygen Consumption and Peak Exercise Minute Ventilation at sea level and high altitude

results.effect_size: Delta VO2 peak: Placebo -32.7, Carvedilol -37.6, Nebivolol -22.5 ml/Kg/min; Delta VE peak: Placebo +0.7, Carvedilol -9.3, Nebivolol +15.2 L/min
results.target_engagement_evidence: Reductions in heart rate and blood pressure observed across treatment arms
biomarker_changes: Peak VO2 at high altitude (Time 3): Placebo 22.9, Carvedilol 24.0, Nebivolol 28.8 ml/Kg/min
Peak minute ventilation at high altitude (Time 3): Placebo 90.3, Carvedilol 84.5, Nebivolol 92.0 L/min
Delta VO2 (Time1 vs Time3): Nebivolol showed smallest decline (-22.5 ml/Kg/min) vs Carvedilol (-37.6) and Placebo (-32.7), p<0.05
Delta VE (Time1 vs Time3): Nebivolol showed largest increase (+15.2 L/min) vs Carvedilol (-9.3) and Placebo (+0.7), p<0.05
subgroup_findings: At high altitude (Time 3), nebivolol preserved peak VO2 better than carvedilol or placebo
Carvedilol was associated with greater decline in peak VO2 at altitude than placebo
Nebivolol was associated with increased minute ventilation at altitude; carvedilol with decreased minute ventilation
safety_signals: No specific safety signals reported in posted results

dose_info.schedule: Carvedilol twice daily; Nebivolol once daily

context.indication: Hypoxia / high altitude exposure in healthy subjects
context.duration: 3 weeks treatment at sea level followed by high altitude exposure

features.level: sea level after three weeks of treatment
